liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Dark Star** (1 review): The performance of Dark Star is highlighted as a strong moment in the set [4]

## Setlist highlights

- **gd69-02-14 t01 Good Morning Little Schoolgirl**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [15]
- **gd69-02-14 t02 Ladies and Gentlemen that's Bear**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [15]
- **gd69-02-14 t03 Dark Star**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [15]
- **gd69-02-14 t04 St. Stephen**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [15]
- **gd69-02-14 t05 The Eleven**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [15]
- **gd69-02-14 t06 Turn On Your Lovelight**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [15]
- **gd69-02-14 t07 Morning Dew**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [15]
- **gd69-02-14 t08 Cryptical Envelopment**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [15]

## The recordings

- **gd1969-02-14.141006.sbd.pcm.dalton.miller.clugston.flac1644** (recommended): soundboard; 11 songs; 114 min; rated 5/5 by 2 [1]. Said about its sound: The first few notes of Good Morning Little Schoolgirl are clipped; The beginning of Dark Star is clipped, and an anomaly in Schoolgirl was minimized [1]
- **gd69-02-14.sbd.cotsman.6286.sbeok.shnf**: soundboard; 10 songs; 111 min; rated 3.22/5 by 9 [2]. Said about its sound: The audio quality is described as slightly muffled despite the overall performance quality; Constant hiss is present, though all instruments remain audible and distinct; Channels are clear with wonderful band interplay, though the recording itself is not the greatest [4][5][9][13]
- **gd1969-02-14.178834.sbd.spc.daniel.flac1644**: soundboard; 9 songs; 109 min [3]

## Around the show

- The band may have played in Philadelphia for the first time on this date [6]
- The reviewer, familiar with the Electric Factory, feels they can almost hear the venue [9]
- The reviewer recalls seeing the band in a small venue, describing the experience as magical [11]
- The late 60s Electric Factory was located on 22nd and Arch, not North 7th [12]
- The performance shows the seeds of the later Live Dead version with shimmering intensity [8]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1969-02-14.141006.sbd.pcm.dalton.miller.clugston.flac1644**: taped by Tim Dalton; transferred by Scott Clugston and Charlie Miller; source: Source Info: Master Soundboard Cassette > Reel to Reel > PCM (Sony HG tape); Transfer Info: PCM (Sony SL-10)> Sony PCM-601ESD > Behringer Ultramatch Pro >… [1]
- **gd69-02-14.sbd.cotsman.6286.sbeok.shnf**: transferred by Jim Hale and J. Cotsman; source: Soundboard [2]
- **gd1969-02-14.178834.sbd.spc.daniel.flac1644**: source: This is an speed corrected remaster of shn=141006 edited by Daniel August 9th, 2026 [3]

## Art and photos

- Poster by LiveGRATEFUL.net: [Grateful Dead 1969-02-14 Fri Valentine's Day Electric Factory, Philadelphia, PA](https://www.livegrateful.net/post/1119599895214/grateful-dead-february-14-1969-electric) [16]
